newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Australian PM Howard hails air pact with Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM Howard hails air pact with Singapore.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said an agreement to boost air links with Singapore was a good deal that would bring economic benefits to both nations.
"It really is a first-class agreement and will have economic benefits for both Singapore and Australia," Howard told reporters.
Howard, on a two-day visit to Singapore, spoke after a meeting with Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) said in a statement that the new arrangements would bring a 37.5 percent increase in passenger service capacity for the airlines of both countries up to 1999.
This would mean an extra 15 Boeing 747 services per week for each side.
The CAAS said the agreement would also more than double freighter flights from 4.5 to 12 Boeing 747 services per week.
Asked to quantify any likely impact on exports, Howard said it was hard to estimate, but that anything that doubled freighter services was bound to be significant.
Goh said the deal would strengthen relations between the two nations in several ways, but most notably would "lead to further tourism and contacts".
Singapore has a Singapore $285.0 million (US$180 million) strategy to turn itself into a tourism hub.

In December, the CAAS unveiled plans for a S$1.5 billion third terminal at Changi Airport that would take passenger capacity to 64 million by 2004 and give the airport facilities to handle the next generation 600-seater super jumbo jets.
Singapore Airlines and Qantas were seen by the CAAS as the two principal corporate beneficiaries of the deal as they are the only Singapore and Australian carriers operating the route at present.

Singapore has already announced open-skies pacts with New Zealand and the United States this year. The U.S. deal, signed in January, was seen as a ground-breaking move as it was the first to be concluded in Asia.
